angle: DL/EDGE: pass-rush-drill get-off burst and Run-the-Hoop bend (Hoop G), year-standardized, against NFL get-off (NGS season), NFL first-second burst, a new NFL bend measure (sideways g in a fixed 2 s window on random sampled rushes) and career pressure rate; baseline = log pick + weight + EDGE share + NGS athleticism + official 10-yd split + 3-cone, leave-one-class-out
metric_name: Hoop G: hardest 0.5 s of sideways (centripetal) acceleration on the Run-the-Hoop lap, g, z within Combine year (contrast: rush-drill burst, yards in the first second of the pass-rush drill)
headline_number: One pre-set margin of 0.5 pressure-rate pts per sd (2.25 pressures per 450-rush season). Beyond the no-tracking baseline (n=77, 30+ NFL rushes): burst -0.05 pts/sd [-0.40, 0.26], 98% inside the margin, ruled out; Hoop G 0.55 [0.24, 0.88] (2.5 pressures/season), 64% above the margin. Held-out: Hoop G R2 gain 0.06 [-0.19, 0.27], rank rho 0.28 -> 0.37, held-out residual rho 0.16 [-0.04, 0.35], positive in 3/3 classes. Baseline held-out R2 -0.02 (pick+role only 0.10). Day-3 shortlist 9/15 (60%) vs rest 15/32 (47%), base rate 51%, gap +13 [-12, 35]. Pre-registered 2026 slope test power 60% (1 class) / 94% (3).
what_changed_from_previous: New candidate in the DL Hoop G lineage (best earlier: round 14 cand_1 8.25; round 16 cand_1 7.75; round 16 cand_3 8.19), applying the round-16 judges' transferable top_changes. (1) One headline margin (0.5 pts/sd, converted to pressures and expected points) used everywhere: in the lede, Fig 1 and the burst equivalence call. (2) Baseline reported with held-out R2, RMSE and rank rho (Table 1), and the drill increments as delta-R2 with class-stratified bootstrap intervals that refit every fold; it states plainly that the baseline is weak (R2 -0.02) and the Hoop G gain includes zero. (3) The forecast is now fit on all 30+ rush linemen, so it is calibrated for day 3 (base rate 51%, not ~30%); the earlier 8/15 vs 8/32 gap shrinks to 9/15 vs 15/32 and is reported with Wilson intervals against the base rate. (4) Simulated 2026 power for both tests; the powered continuous slope test (60%/94%) is pre-registered as primary instead of the underpowered hit-rate test (9%), with an explicit 'what would change the call'. (5) New in-game bend measure in a fixed 2 s window (avoids pressured snaps being longer by construction); a drill-to-game transfer matrix (Fig 3) with noise ceilings; snap-level fixed-effects odds ratios for get-off and bend turned into a 4-item film checklist that replaces splits. (6) The lede defines Hoop G and burst before stating the numbers in ~60 words; analyst machinery is in the appendix; 2025 shortlist with go/no-go calls and the lede names Sawyer (go), Brinson (go), Ingram-Dawkins (no-go). (7) The script renders the writeup from a template, so every number comes from numbers.json.
open_risks: The held-out R2 gain for Hoop G includes zero (0.06 [-0.19, 0.27]); the 0.55 slope interval comes from training-fold fits, and the case rests on consistency across 3 classes rather than size
Hoop G was chosen after earlier rounds screened several drill measures on these same classes; holding classes out does not correct that search, and 2026 is the first clean test
Hoop G reliability rests on 10 linemen with two laps (0.37); 91% have one lap

The NFL bend measure has no blockers in the data and may partly be a result of winning the rep rather than a cause; Hoop G -> NFL bend is only 0.14 [-0.04, 0.31], so the mechanism is mostly unexplained
Go calls for Sawyer and Brinson rest on 173-176 rushes and small margins over forecast (0.6-0.9 pts); Biggers is labelled Go at +0.2 pts by the mechanical rule
The no-tracking baseline overfits (held-out R2 -0.02 vs 0.10 for pick+role); judges may prefer the pick-only model as the comparator
Full run takes ~6 minutes because of 2,000 bootstrap refits
